key_impacts: Nuclear fuel melted inside multiple reactors
Extremely contaminated coolant water leaked into reactor building basements
Site filled with numerous 1,000‑ton tanks storing contaminated water
About 400 tons of groundwater flow into the site daily, worsening contamination
evidence_snippets: Large-scale nuclear disaster at TEPCO’s Fukushima Daiichi, directly caused by the Great East Japan Earthquake and Tsunami of March 11, 2011.
The fuel melted inside the nuclear reactors due to the accident.
Coolant water becomes extremely contaminated; ~400 tons of groundwater flow in daily, filling 1,000‑ton tanks on site.
missing_information: Casualty and evacuation figures not provided in the excerpt
